staticText: Neutral haemoglobin inheritance education only. The tool may cross two user-selected, lab-confirmed AA, AS, AC, SS, SC, or CC results in a four-cell Punnett model and show genotype probabilities for each pregnancy. Each pregnancy is independent; percentages cannot predict or guarantee an individual child’s genotype. AS is sickle cell trait and differs from sickle cell disease; SS and SC are sickle cell disease patterns; AC is haemoglobin C trait; CC is haemoglobin C disease, not sickle cell disease. The tool must not label people or relationships compatible, safe, dangerous, high risk, or unsuitable; direct relationship or reproductive decisions; diagnose or confirm a genotype; interpret symptoms or severity; recommend testing, prenatal procedures, treatment, or assisted reproduction; or claim population burden, prevalence, price, prognosis, or cure. It does not cover beta-thalassaemia or haemoglobin variants beyond A, S, and C. Users should use qualified laboratory results and discuss testing, newborn screening, confirmatory follow-up, and personal questions with a clinician or genetic counsellor. Selected genotypes remain in the browser and are not stored or sent to AI, analytics, email, a profile, a share URL, or a server. Print-to-PDF and text export are local and ungated. Official context checked 2026-07-26: CDC About Sickle Cell Disease, CDC Sickle Cell Trait, NIH/NHLBI Sickle Cell Trait, and NIH/NHLBI Pregnancy and Reproduction.
